newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian ruling Socialists discuss Dobrev for PM.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian ruling Socialists discuss Dobrev for PM.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party on Wednesday began discussing with parliamentary allies the nomination of powerful Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev to replace Zhan Videnov who resigned as prime minister last month.
Socialist party chairman Georgi Parvanov told reporters the party would seek a broad support for Dobrev who has yet to be approved by parliament.
If approved, Dobrev would hand his mandate to form a new cabinet to outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev and meet President -Elect Petar Stoyanov who is due to take office on January 19, said Parvanov.
Political analysts said Dobrev's nomination may be opposed by some Socialist deputies who fear his access to information might endanger their careers.
Bulgarian police files from the communist era have never been made public as they were in East Germany.
Analaysts said Dobrev was likely to pass the vote by a narrow margin.
Videnov resigned at a Socialist congress in December after months of criticism of his handling of the economy, sparking a showdown between party hardliners and reformists.

Dobrev, 49, emerged as an outspoken critic of Videnov at the congress. He attacked the cabinet's record in handling Bulgaria's economic and social crisis and raised the previously taboo issue of government corruption.
The BSP is expected to discuss a new cabinet at a plenum on Sunday.
"Some of the ministers in the current cabinet will probably retain their posts in the new cabinet," said BSP's Lyubomir Kolarov.
